first.rationale: Simplifying onboarding directly addresses the 4% completion decline and may also recover activation, with prior evidence of durable early-adoption gains. Promotional pricing is the most relevant alternative given competitor pressure, but its reported 30-day retention harm conflicts with the sustainable qualified-revenue objective; verify that downside alongside the onboarding evidence before committing.

mid.rationale: Run a standard experiment simplifying onboarding. The verified source directly matches the current onboarding decline and showed completion +13%, time-to-value improved by 2.1 days, and 30-day retention +3%, aligning with sustainable qualified revenue. Promotional pricing is rejected despite acquisition gains because verified retention fell 12% and the cohort failed to survive first renewal. A controlled experiment preserves uncertainty about whether the prior onboarding effect will replicate under current conditions.

final2.rationale: Proceed with onboarding simplification despite the competitor's deeper price cut. Verified evidence shows completion +13%, time-to-value improved by 2.1 days, and 30-day retention +3%, directly addressing current onboarding and activation weakness while supporting sustainable revenue. Promotional pricing is not selected because the verified 40% discount produced 30-day retention -12% and cohorts failed to survive first renewal; escalating price pressure does not remove that downstream-value risk. Use a standard controlled experiment because replication under current market conditions remains uncertain.
